defects.canonical: next_cursor is set to window[-1]['id'], the id of the last item INCLUDED in the current page. On the next call bisect_left(ids, cursor) lands on that same item's index, so combined with the inclusive start (d2) the boundary item is re-served as the first row of the next page. Even on its own, advertising the last-returned id as the next cursor only works if the start is exclusive; here it is not.
defects.why_subtle: Returning the last item's id as the next cursor is the textbook keyset idiom; the off-by-one only manifests when paired with the inclusive bisect_left start.

defects.canonical: The docstring states the cursor is EXCLUSIVE (page starts strictly after it), but bisect_left(ids, cursor) returns the index OF the cursor element when present, so window[start:] INCLUDES the cursor item. Exclusive semantics require bisect_right (or start+1) so the matched id is skipped.
defects.why_subtle: bisect_left vs bisect_right reads as an arbitrary, both-plausible choice; the reader rarely checks it against the exclusive contract stated three lines up in the docstring.

defects.canonical: page() rebuilds the full ids list via [it['id'] for it in items] on every call, an O(N) scan of the whole collection per page, so a paged walk is O(N*pages) rather than O(N). The id list (or an index) should be built once.
defects.why_subtle: the comprehension is a single clean line that looks like setup, but it runs on every paginated call and turns a keyset walk quadratic.
